product: COMIRNATY (COVID-19 Vaccine, mRNA) single-dose vials — ultra-low-temperature storage condition
storage_and_handling_verbatim: Alternatively, single-dose vials may be stored in an ultra-low temperature freezer at -90ºC to -60ºC (-130ºF to -76ºF). Do not store vials at -25°C to -15°C (-13°F to 5°F).
source_document: FDA-approved full prescribing information for COMIRNATY, Section 16 HOW SUPPLIED/STORAGE AND HANDLING, "Storage Prior to Use — Single-Dose Vials". Document footer LAB-1490-16.2, revised 8/2026.
excursion_band_note: Deliberately absent. The label states no permitted EXCURSION envelope around the ULT band — it states separate alternative STORAGE conditions (2-8 °C for up to 10 weeks once thawed; 8-25 °C total time out of refrigeration not to exceed 12 h), and explicitly forbids -25 to -15 °C for these vials. Treating an alternative storage condition as an excursion envelope would invent a stability claim the label does not make, so the storage band is scored on its own and coldcall's beyond-envelope rule stays inactive.
allowance_source: ColdCall benchmark assumption (12 h) anchored to the only cumulative time-out-of-condition figure the COMIRNATY label states — NOT a ULT stability budget
provenance: The -90 to -60 °C band is published label text, quoted verbatim above from the FDA prescribing information retrieved 2026-08-28 (md5 55edfece518bdd227371ea04276a2f19 of the PDF at the source_url). The excursion ALLOWANCE HOURS in config.json are NOT from this or any label: real thermal-stability budgets for this product are manufacturer data that is not published. See config.json's policy_note.
not_regulatory_validation: Scoring recorded container-test thermocouples against this label band is a benchmark of the arithmetic, not a regulatory disposition of any vaccine lot. The recordings are dry-ice packages in a laboratory refrigerated-container test at ORNL/Carrier; no vaccine was present.
